text: Stomach ulcers are common in sows and fattening pigs. Signs: not eating but no fever, pale skin (reflecting internal stomach bleeding), constipation with dark feces (digested blood), and vomiting. Causes: insufficient fiber in the diet, or poor-quality raw materials. Treatment: distribute feed 4–5 times a day, mixed with water into a doughy consistency; offer fresh forage; and inject an appetite-stimulating product along with Vitamin B12 to counter anemia. Add wheat bran to raise fiber content as a fix for the underlying cause.
